settings.configWorkspaces.title: Settings and workspaces
settings.wizard.title: Setup wizard
wizard.title: Setup wizard
wizard.subtitle.first: Let us set Coxia up for the way you work. It opens with the language and the name, and every step after it, up to the review, can be skipped and picked up again later.
wizard.subtitle.rerun: Review or redo the configuration of this workspace. What you already set up stays in place.
wizard.web.title: Finish the setup in the desktop app
wizard.web.body: This installation has not been set up yet. The wizard opens in the app window, on the computer where Coxia is installed. Once it is finished there, come back to this page.
wizard.web.secrets: Keys and tokens are never typed in the browser: they stay on the computer.
wizard.step.language.hint: Pick the app language and what the agents should call you.
wizard.step.models.hint: Add the model providers, test the connection and say which model does each job.
wizard.step.sdk.hint: Claude providers run through Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK. It is installed in a folder of yours, with your consent.
wizard.step.projects.hint: Say where your repositories live. Coxia finds the git repositories and their remotes by itself.
wizard.step.integrations.hint: Connect GitLab, GitHub or Bitbucket to read issues, merge requests and pipelines.
wizard.step.docs.hint: Where the agents find context: CLAUDE.md, skills, rules, agents, knowledge base and MCP.
wizard.step.cycle.hint: Choose the model of your work cycle and see which ceremonies appear.
wizard.step.voice.hint: Voice is optional: without it the ceremonies happen in text.
wizard.step.review.hint: Check the summary. You can export the configuration and redo any step later, in Settings.
wizard.problem.noProvider: Add at least one model provider.
wizard.problem.roleModel: Every role needs a provider and a model (no spaces).
wizard.problem.repoId: A repository short name uses lowercase letters, digits, "-" and "_".
wizard.problem.repoDuplicate: Two repositories share the same short name. Change one of them.
wizard.problem.vcsHost: Every integration needs a host, such as gitlab.example.com.
wizard.language.name: What should the agents call you?
wizard.language.nameHint: Optional. The agents use the name when they talk to you. It stays in this workspace.
wizard.language.importHint: Import the file exported from another computer or workspace. You see everything it changes before applying.
wizard.language.importHintRerun: Import a configuration file into this workspace or into a new one. You see everything it changes before applying.
wizard.secret.storedSecure: It is encrypted with the system keychain and is never exported.
wizard.secret.storedInsecure: It is kept in a local file with restricted permissions (0600), unencrypted, and is never exported.
wizard.secret.noKeychain: This computer has no system keychain. Prefer an environment variable or a command, or accept keeping it in a local unencrypted file (permission 0600).
wizard.secret.acceptInsecure: Keep in a local unencrypted file
wizard.secret.envHint: The value is read from the variable when needed; Coxia only keeps the name.
wizard.secret.commandHint: Runs without a shell, with the arguments you write (for example your password manager). Coxia only keeps the command.
wizard.secret.problem.empty: Fill in the value before saving.
wizard.secret.problem.bad-env-name: Invalid variable name: use letters, digits and "_".
wizard.models.noSubscription: Coxia uses an API key or your cloud credentials. A claude.ai subscription login is not offered: Anthropic does not allow third-party apps to offer it.
wizard.models.noModelNoAgent: Without a model provider no agent runs: this step is where the app is set up to talk to one.
wizard.kind.anthropic.hint: Claude models straight from the Anthropic API. Create an API key in the Anthropic console.
wizard.kind.bedrock.hint: Claude models through AWS. Uses this machine's AWS credentials, or a Bedrock API token.
wizard.kind.vertex.hint: Claude models through Google Cloud. Uses this machine's Google application default credentials.
wizard.kind.foundry.hint: Claude models through Microsoft Foundry. Uses a resource key or this machine's Azure login.
wizard.kind.openai-compatible.hint: Any OpenAI-style API: cloud (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek) or local (Ollama, LM Studio). Runs on Coxia's open engine.
wizard.models.baseUrlHint: Ends in /v1 on most servers. You may paste just the address, such as http://localhost:11434.
wizard.models.modelHint: Optional. The connection test lists the models the server offers.
wizard.models.localHint: Local server: no key needed. The test checks the context size: the agent prompt is over 10 thousand tokens, and Ollama defaults to 4096 (raise num_ctx).
wizard.models.bedrockRegionHint: The AWS region where the models are enabled, for example us-east-1.
wizard.models.awsProfileHint: Name of a profile in the AWS credentials file. Empty: the default chain (environment variables, ~/.aws, machine role).
wizard.models.bedrockCreds: The AWS credentials come from the machine itself (aws configure, environment variables or an IAM role). Coxia only keeps the region and the profile.
wizard.models.useToken: Use a Bedrock API token instead of AWS credentials
wizard.models.vertexRegionHint: For example global or us-east5, where the Claude models are enabled.
wizard.models.vertexCreds: Sign in with gcloud auth application-default login on this machine. Coxia only keeps the project and the region.
wizard.models.foundryResourceHint: The name of the Azure resource, which appears in the address https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com.
wizard.models.foundryCreds: Use a resource key, or leave the key out and sign in with az login on this machine.
wizard.models.openEngineNote: This provider runs on the open engine (Coxia's own agent loop): it reads, writes inside the run's worktree and runs commands under the same safety policy as the Claude Agent SDK. Quality depends on the model you pick.
wizard.models.problem.baseUrl: The base URL must start with http:// or https://.
wizard.models.problem.vertex: Enter the Google Cloud project and region.
wizard.models.keyUnavailable: The key source is not available on this computer
wizard.models.removeLast: At least one provider must stay.
wizard.models.testFail.sdk-missing: Testing Claude providers uses the Claude Agent SDK, which is not installed yet. Install it in the next step and test again.
wizard.models.testFail.no-key: This provider has no key. Set the key and test again.
wizard.models.testFail.failed: The provider answered with an error.
wizard.models.testFail.unreachable: The provider could not be reached.
wizard.models.listed: {count} models listed by the server: pick them in the roles below.
wizard.models.sdkAnswered: The model answered a short call through the Claude Agent SDK, with the environment the agents would use.
wizard.warn.no-chat: The model did not answer a simple prompt.
wizard.warn.no-tools: This model does not call tools, and the ceremonies need them to read files and return structured answers. Prefer another model.
wizard.warn.small-context: Small context window (under 12 thousand tokens): the agent prompt alone is over 10 thousand. Raise the context on the server or use a bigger model.
wizard.warn.tiny-context: Tiny context window (under 6 thousand tokens): the ceremonies will not fit. Raise the context (on Ollama, num_ctx) or choose another model.
wizard.warn.no-json-schema: The server does not accept response_format json_schema; Coxia uses a final tool or the prompt to get the JSON.
wizard.warn.untested: Not tested yet: run the connection test to see what this provider can do.
wizard.models.rolesHint: The most frequent roles want fast, cheap models; the unblock role deserves a stronger one.
wizard.role.turn.hint: Builds each item's turn. It is the most called role: a fast, cheap model.
wizard.role.reply.hint: Understands your answer and extracts the decision and the action.
wizard.role.deep.hint: Investigates in depth, reading specs, issues and documentation. Worth a stronger model.
wizard.role.teams.hint: Writes the summaries for the team's daily.
wizard.role.fix.hint: Fixes diagrams and checks short answers. A cheap model is enough.
wizard.sdk.bundled: The Claude Agent SDK already ships with this app.
wizard.sdk.bundledHint: This installation uses the bundled copy. Nothing to install.
wizard.sdk.local: Claude Agent SDK installed on this machine.
wizard.sdk.termsBody: The Claude Agent SDK is Anthropic software with its own terms. Coxia downloads the package from npm into a folder of yours; its use is subject to the terms below.
wizard.sdk.noSubscription: API keys or cloud credentials only: the claude.ai subscription login is not offered.
wizard.sdk.accept: I read the terms and want to install the SDK
wizard.sdk.acceptHint: Installs with npm into {dir}. Nothing is installed system-wide.
wizard.sdk.npmMissing: npm was not found. Install Node.js (nodejs.org), reopen the app and try again.
wizard.sdk.notLanded: npm finished, but the SDK did not show up in the install folder.
wizard.sdk.skipHint: You may skip: without the SDK the Claude providers will not work until you install it (Settings → Wizard).
wizard.projects.rootsHint: Folders that hold your repositories. The first one is where the agents work.
wizard.projects.pickTitle: Choose a projects folder or a repository
wizard.projects.autoDiscoverHint: Treats any git repository directly inside those folders as a project.
wizard.projects.empty: Add a folder for Coxia to look for repositories. With no projects the agents work in the workspace folder.
wizard.projects.noneFound: No git repository found in those folders (up to two levels deep).
wizard.projects.repoIdHint: Shown on cards and in prompts.
wizard.projects.hostUnknown: This remote's address was not recognised: create the integration in the next step and pick it here.
wizard.projects.unmapped: {count} repository(ies) point to {host}, which has no integration yet.
wizard.vcs.intro: Integrations are optional and read-only: issues, merge requests and pipelines. Writes always go through your approval.
wizard.vcs.none: No integration yet. Without them Coxia does not fetch issues or merge requests.
wizard.vcs.hostGithub: github.com, or the address of your GitHub Enterprise Server.
wizard.vcs.userHint: Only to identify the account in notices.
wizard.vcs.userBitbucket: On Bitbucket Cloud with an API token, enter the account e-mail; with no user the token is sent as a Bearer.
wizard.vcs.apiUrlHint: Empty: derived from the host (GitLab /api/v4, GitHub api.github.com or /api/v3). Fill it in if your server uses another path or http.
wizard.vcs.createToken: Create a token at this address
wizard.vcs.scopes.gitlab: Personal access token with the read_api scope (reading issues, merge requests and pipelines) and read_repository. Do not grant api or write_repository: Coxia does not need to write.
wizard.vcs.scopes.github: Fine-grained token limited to the repositories that matter, with Metadata, Contents, Issues and Pull requests read-only (and Actions if you want pipelines). On a classic token the repo scope is enough but broader.
wizard.vcs.scopes.bitbucket: API token (or repository token) with read access to repositories, pull requests, issues and pipelines. Avoid write permissions.
wizard.vcs.scopesNote: The token is kept like the model keys (on this computer, environment variable or command) and is never exported.
wizard.vcs.test.noToken: No token: enter and save it before testing.
wizard.vcs.test.timeout: The server did not answer in time.
wizard.vcs.test.401: The token was refused (401). Check its value and expiry.
wizard.vcs.test.403: The token lacks permission (403). Check its scopes.
wizard.vcs.test.404: API address not found (404). Check the host.
wizard.vcs.fallbackNote: Minimal test: it only reads the current user through the REST API.
wizard.vcs.issuesHint: The project that holds the activity issues. Without it there are no cards coming from the tracker.
wizard.vcs.issuesPrefixHint: Optional, like app# in app#101. Empty: just the number.
wizard.vcs.issuesScopeHint: Only open issues. The cards of code changes stay the ones you opened or were asked to review.
wizard.vcs.issuesScope.all: All open issues of the issue project
wizard.vcs.issuesScope.labels: Open issues with any of these labels
wizard.vcs.issuesLabelsHint: Separated by commas. An issue needs only one of them.
wizard.vcs.issuesScopeNote.noProject: Without the issue project above this choice does not apply yet: until it is set, only the issues assigned to you become cards.
wizard.vcs.issuesScopeNote.noLabels: No label is listed: until some are, only the issues assigned to you become cards.
wizard.vcs.issuesScopeNote.noLabelSuppor: The issue tracker of this integration has no labels: only the issues assigned to you become cards.
wizard.vcs.issuesScopeNote.external: A card source command is on: it decides which cards exist, so this choice does not apply.
wizard.docs.claudeMdRoots.hint: Folders whose CLAUDE.md goes into the agents' context.
wizard.docs.skillsDirs.hint: Folders with one subfolder per skill (each with a SKILL.md).
wizard.docs.rulesDirs.hint: Folders with project rules, read on demand.
wizard.docs.mcpConfigFiles.hint: .mcp.json files with MCP servers (local stdio servers only).
wizard.docs.sourceScanner: Found by the agent preparation scan.
wizard.docs.sourceFallback: Found by a simple search for .claude/, CLAUDE.md and .mcp.json in your projects and in ~/.claude.
wizard.docs.autoDetectHint: Adds to what is listed what the ceremonies' agents would load from Claude Code by itself (~/.claude and the .claude folder and CLAUDE.md of each project), and the .mcp.json of each project for every agent. The agents of runs, mentions and conversations do not read the Claude Code files: they read the .coxia folder of each repository.
wizard.docs.specsDirHint: Folder with one subfolder per issue (specs, plans, quizzes). Empty: Coxia writes no spec files.
wizard.docs.specsNote: The agents may read and write documents in this folder during the gates.
wizard.cycle.placeholder: The ready-made cycle templates are not in this build yet. For now you choose which ceremonies are on.
wizard.cycle.tpl.none.hint: Just the voice or text conversation: no stages and no spec structure.
wizard.cycle.tpl.sdd.hint: Review gates over specs, plans and QA.
wizard.cycle.ceremoniesHint: Turn off the ones that make no sense for your team.
wizard.cer.preDaily.hint: One agent per item tells what changed, before the daily.
wizard.cer.unblock.hint: Investigates a blocked item in depth.
wizard.cer.gate.hint: A consolidation quiz over specs and plans before moving on.
wizard.cer.qaHandoff.hint: Prepares the hand-off of the item to QA. Needs a QA user and a cycle with stages.
wizard.cer.retro.hint: A weekly conversation on what worked and what did not.
wizard.cer.releaseConflicts.hint: Resolves merge conflicts after a release. Needs a configured sync command.
wizard.cycle.stagesHint: How to recognise each stage from the issue status. Case-insensitive regular expressions, separated by commas.
wizard.cycle.noTracker: With no issue integration configured, the stages have no effect.
wizard.voice.onHint: The agents speak and you answer by speaking.
wizard.voice.offHint: The ceremonies become text conversations. No microphone and no speech synthesis.
wizard.voice.engine.edge.hint: Sounds more natural and is light on the machine.
wizard.voice.engine.kokoro.hint: Runs on your computer. Sounds a bit more robotic and the first utterance takes longer.
wizard.voice.edgePrivacy: With the Edge voice, the text the agents speak is sent to Microsoft to be synthesised. To keep everything on the machine, use Kokoro.
wizard.voice.kokoroPrivacy: With Kokoro no spoken text leaves your computer. The transcription of your voice also runs locally.
wizard.voice.sttHint: Bigger is more accurate and slower. small is a good middle ground.
wizard.voice.installed: The voice dependencies were already installed on this machine.
wizard.voice.soon: Automatic voice setup is not in this build yet.
wizard.voice.lazy: If you skip, voice stays off and the ceremonies work by text. You can install it later in Settings › Voice (needs the network).
wizard.review.sdkWarn: Some providers use the Claude Agent SDK and it is not installed: they will not work until it is.
wizard.review.missingSecrets: These keys or tokens have no source yet: {refs}.
wizard.export.hint: Saves this workspace's configuration to a file. It carries no history and no keys: only references, for whoever imports it to provide again.
wizard.import.hint: Pick an exported file. Nothing is written before you check what it changes.
wizard.import.replaceNote: That workspace's current configuration is replaced; the previous one is kept as config.pre-import.json.
wizard.import.invalid: The file is not a valid configuration:
wizard.import.migrated: The file was from an older schema and was converted ({count} adjustment(s)).
wizard.import.commandsHint: A configuration file can make the app run programs. Only apply it if you trust where it came from.
wizard.import.missingPaths: {count} path(s) do not exist on this computer:
wizard.import.secrets: Keys and tokens it asks for
wizard.import.secretsHint: The file never carries values. Provide the source of each one now, or later in the settings.
wizard.import.secretHave: A source for this secret already exists on this computer.
wizard.import.doneNew: Workspace created with the configuration. Use it to open the app in it.
wizard.import.doneOther: Configuration written to the other workspace. Use it to open the app in it.
wizard.settings.webNote: Exporting, importing and opening the wizard only work in the app window on the computer: keys and files never go through the browser.
wizard.settings.wizardHint: Redo the configuration step by step: models, projects, integrations, documentation, cycle and voice.
wizard.settings.open: Open the wizard in this workspace
wizard.settings.newTitle: Or set up a new workspace
wizard.settings.newHint: Creates an empty workspace and restarts the app in it, straight into the wizard. The current workspace is untouched.
wizard.docs.projects: What I found in each project
wizard.cycle.needs: To get the most from this template you still provide: {list}.
wizard.poolMode.title: How a pool is used
wizard.poolMode.intro: This acts where a role or an agent has a list of its own for an activity (reading and searching, editing, commands, the screen). Without one the pool is a reserve only, whatever you pick. Saving such a list starts delegation by itself, unless you pick another mode here. An agent or a stage of the cycle can choose its own.
wizard.poolMode.fallback.hint: One model. The pool enters only when the model in use is busy. A turn on the screen never goes to a model known not to take images.
wizard.poolMode.switch.hint: Each turn goes to the model of the list of its activity; the model in use stays while it reaches the activity's floor. Each switch loses the prompt cache.
wizard.poolMode.delegate.hint: The main model stays fixed and keeps its cache. Editing, commands and the screen go to sub-agents, each on the list of its activity and with only the tools of its kind. Needs the sub-agents switch of the tools (on by default). This is the default.
wizard.pool.hint: When the model above is busy (rate limit, overload or a server error), the call moves to the next one on this list and the stage goes on. Put them from the cheapest to the most expensive. Only models of the providers you added.
wizard.pool.empty: No reserves: the model above is the only one.
wizard.pool.byActivityHint: A list here replaces the reserves for that kind of work, and its first model is the one tried first. Left empty, the list above is used.
wizard.activity.explore.hint: Turns that answer to file reads and searches.
wizard.activity.edit.hint: Turns that answer to file writes and edits.
wizard.activity.shell.hint: Turns that answer to the output of a command.
wizard.activity.screen.hint: Turns that answer to a screenshot. Only models that take images are used.
wizard.activity.write: Start of a stage and documents
wizard.activity.write.hint: The first turn of a stage, the ceremonies, the documents and the closing answers.
wizard.pool.addProvider: Provider of the model to add to “{list}”
wizard.pool.problem.empty: Type the name of the model, without spaces.
wizard.pool.problem.provider: Pick a provider you already added.
wizard.pool.problem.duplicate: That model is already in the list.
wizard.pool.problem.max: A list holds at most 8 models.
wizard.suggest.title: Suggested pool
wizard.suggest.intro: Models in the listing of {provider} that call tools, answer in a structured form and have at least {tokens} tokens of context, in the order of the estimated cost of a typical stage. For the kinds of work that have a quality floor, the models that reach it come first.
wizard.suggest.scoresNote: The scores come from a table that ships with the app, and most are reported by the vendor of each model: they are a floor and a tie-breaker, not a guarantee. Change a floor or a score below if you know better. Nothing is saved until you save.
wizard.suggest.floorsHint: A model under the floor of a kind of work goes after the ones that reach it. Reading and searching and the start of a stage have no floor: the price decides.
wizard.suggest.defaultHint: The start of a stage, the ceremonies and the documents. The first of the list becomes each role's model; today's model stays in the pool, at its place by cost.
wizard.suggest.noCatalog: The listing of {provider} carries no price or capabilities, so there is nothing to suggest from. Add reserves by hand under each role.
wizard.suggest.none: No model in the listing qualifies: it needs tools and structured output not ruled out, and at least {tokens} tokens of known context.
wizard.suggest.useHint: Replaces the model, the reserves and the lists of {roles} in this draft. Nothing is saved until you save.
wizard.suggest.noRoles: No role uses {provider}, so there is nothing to place the suggestion on.
wizard.suggest.placed: The suggestion is in the draft. Review it under each role, then save.
wizard.features.title: Server features
wizard.features.hint: What this server accepts beyond the protocol. Switched on, the request carries the parameter only for the models marked for it (the mark comes from the connection test, and you correct it on the model's row). Switched off, nothing in the request changes.
wizard.features.serviceTier.hint: service_tier "flex": cheaper (20% off) with a longer queue, only on calls nobody waits for (stages, questions between agents); never on a ceremony or an @mention.
wizard.features.failFast: Refuse at once when a model is busy
wizard.features.failFast.hint: fail_fast on every model of a pool but the last, so the pool moves on to the next without waiting in the queue; the last one waits as before.
wizard.features.reasoningEffort.hint: reasoning_effort, for the models that take it. The levels are under "Reasoning effort", below the roles.
wizard.features.catalogUrl: Address of the richer model listing
wizard.features.catalogUrl.hint: Read only by the connection test (flex, retirement dates, tool and schema tags). It must be at the provider's own origin, because the key goes with the request.
wizard.features.problem.scheme: Use an address that starts with http:// or https://.
wizard.features.problem.origin: The address must be at the same origin as the provider's: the key is never sent anywhere else.
wizard.features.preset.hint: Switches on what the preset of this provider brings, and its listing address. Only you switch it on: the app never does it by itself, and it does not touch a provider that has no preset.
wizard.effort.title: Reasoning effort
wizard.effort.intro: How hard a model that reasons is asked to think, per activity. It applies to the models marked "effort" on a provider with the feature on; "The model's own" sends nothing. The main model uses the level of "Start of a stage and documents" on every turn; a sub-agent uses the level of its kind.
wizard.effort.label: Effort for {activity}
wizard.pool.offer.flex.title: Served in the flex tier (cheaper, longer queue). The mark comes from the catalog; click to correct it.
wizard.pool.offer.effort.title: Takes the reasoning effort. The mark comes from the catalog; click to correct it.
wizard.obsolete.title: The provider marks models you use as obsolete. Nothing is changed for you.
